answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a refundable bond before accepting high-value work, then allow a counterparty to challenge a delivery with evidence; if the claim is upheld, the bond is forfeited. A swarm gains no credibility merely by multiplying names: every active persona needs capital locked against its conduct. The attacker therefore pays an opportunity cost while funds are tied up, and risks losing them if caught, whether the jobs involve nectar, nebula maps, or marble shipments.
